The two deleted rows ARE the connections: L012750 (5A-4-SM-MH917 -> 5A-1-FL-STP, 10,469 m) and L012751 (5A-5-TM-MH1759 -> 5A-1-FL-STP, 5,648 m). FORCELINE_IBRI.shp holds exactly one STATUS=='Ex' record, L021671, OD250, 9,994 m: start 4.9 m from 5A-1-FL-SPS, end 0.6 m from 5A-1-FL-STP (and 5.8 m from the project's recorded STP at E444422.8 N2563337.9; the SPS end is 3.0 m from the recorded PS at E449899.59 N2567301.72). Per package components = 1 for all five: CONFIRMED. Component sizes 1,123/32.25 km (5A-1), 988/28.51 km (5A-2+3+4), 1,154/34.70 km (5A-5): CONFIRMED. Nesting 5A-3 -> 5A-2-TM-MH79 and 5A-2 -> 5A-4-TM-MH6033: CONFIRMED. Pipes leaving each package (robust parse): 5A-1 = **0**, 5A-2 = 1, 5A-3 = 1, 5A-4 = 0, 5A-5 = 0.
design_rule: KEEP the package-level gate: one construction package = one connected component with exactly one outlet; publish component count and terminal count per package every run. DROP the inference that W11b's 18 subnetworks stopping short of the main pipe fail a test NAMA passes. NAMA's own 5A-1 gravity tree - 32.25 km, a third of the built network - stops 6,754 m short of the STP and is closed by a pumping station and a 10 km rising main. The correct test is not 'does gravity reach the main pipe' but 'is every terminal either the main pipe or a pumping station with a designed rising main'.
copy_or_not: COPY (the per-package one-tree-one-outlet gate). DO NOT copy the 'three separate systems' framing or the criticism of subnetworks that terminate at a pump.
correction: The built network is ONE system with ONE final outlet - the STP at 5A-1-FL-STP - made of three gravity trees joined by three pressure mains. The third component exists only because the analyst's own >100 m-per-vertex filter deleted two of those pressure mains from the graph before counting components. The third is L021671 in FORCELINE_IBRI.shp, which the analyst never opened. Separately, '1 exit pipe for 5A-1' is wrong (it is 0) and is an artifact of the claimed regex ^(pkg)-(zone)-MH(digits)$, which fails on 435 of 3,267 manhole IDs - every one of them in 5A-1, affecting 678 of 3,265 pipes (20.8%) - not the '1 unparsed' the method section states. A loose parse that requires only '-MH' fails on exactly one ID (5A-1-FL-SPS).

design_rule: A lateral must reach a sub main or trunk within 2 zone hops (4 at the 90th percentile, 5 absolute maximum) and within about 335 m median / 683 m p90 of travel through lateral-tier pipe MEASURED PER ZONE. If the check is written per pipe instead, the band is 258 m / 603 m - state which unit the gate uses. Publish the chain-depth histogram per subnetwork every run; a long tail means the main tier is missing.
copy_or_not: COPY, with the travel band corrected and the unit stated.
correction: The claim silently switches denominator between its two halves: depth is aggregated per zone over 582 zones, but the metres are per pipe over 2,798 pipes, while the method section says both are 'taken per zone as the worst of its own pipes'. Applied per zone - the unit every other part of the claim uses - the travel band is 335 m median / 683 m p90 outside 5A-1, about 30 % higher than the 250 m / 600 m the rule proposes. A design gate set at 250/600 would fail roughly a third of NAMA's own zones. Second, the p90 of 3 is pooled over four packages: 5A-2's own p90 is 4 and every max-5 zone is in 5A-2, so a per-subnetwork gate of 3 is tighter than the built network.

design_rule: Target roughly 3 in 4 lateral zones feeding another lateral, 1 in 5 feeding a sub main, 1 in 20 reaching the trunk, and never quote the ratio without saying whether an unlabelled package is in the pool. Correct AS_BUILT_TARGETS.md line 119 to 73.2 % on 272 exits from 4 packages - and change the band from a floor to a window (about 60-78 %, the measured per-package range), because '>= 87.69' rewards a design for drifting toward 5A-1.
copy_or_not: COPY
correction: The correction to 73.2 % holds and is robust to whether you count exits or zones. Two refinements. (a) The pooled figure is 87.69 % (520 of 593), not the 87.5 % (519) the claim computes - the claim drops the 5A-1-FL-SPS exit as unparsed, so the record's 87.69 % was computed correctly and the claim's own recomputation is the outlier. The stated denominator is the zone count; the actual denominator is 593 exits. Fix both the value and the denominator label. claim: Joins onto the trunk are held at about 4.6 per km, but the single figure hides a fourfold spread between packages - 5A-5 runs at 11.7 joins per km because its trunk is only 510 m long.

design_rule: Cap direct joins onto the trunk at about 4-5 per km of trunk and onto the whole main tier at about 5 per km, measured per subnetwork. Where a trunk is shorter than about 1 km, judge it on absolute joins (0-8 is the built range) rather than per km. Report the per-package range 0.00-11.72 alongside the 4.64, not a fourfold spread.
copy_or_not: COPY, with the range corrected and the sample size published beside the target.

claim: A sub main is defined by ROUTE, not by a load threshold. Four of ten begin fronting zero plots, eight begin already carrying an inherited load, more than half of sub-main length fronts nothing, and the load ranges of the two tiers overlap heavily.

RADIUS SWEEP - SUBMAIN no-frontage share is 64.6 % at 30 m, 53.1 % at 60 m, 50.0 % at 100 m, **48.4 % at 150 m**. Sub-main outlet loads 48.8-1,398.9, median 311.5. Lateral outlets excl 5A-1 median 11.6, p90 64.0, max 223.5; all 582 median 17.4, max 3,027.8. 151 of 582 (44 of 270 outside 5A-1) exceed the smallest sub-main outlet of 48.8. Lateral zones collected directly per sub main: **2 to 15** (5A-5|SM.1 15, 5A-5|SM.2 11 lateral + 1 sub main, 5A-5|SM.4 only 2). 5A-5|SM.3 -> SM.2 and 5A-4|SM.6 -> the system outlet chamber: CONFIRMED.
design_rule: Define the sub-main tier by ROUTE - the corridor that carries several lateral zones to the trunk - and let the diameter follow the accumulated flow. Do not trigger a tier change on a property count. Expect a sub main to collect 2-15 lateral zones and to front plots on roughly half its length (48-65 % fronting nothing, depending on how generously you allocate). Every load figure here is an allocation output, not a measurement: publish the radius with the number.
copy_or_not: COPY (the route-not-threshold conclusion). The load figures are INFORM_ONLY - they move 20-40 % across a plausible allocation radius.
correction: The core conclusion - a sub main is a route, not a load threshold - survives every correction and survives the radius sweep intact; the tier load ranges overlap at 30, 60, 100 and 150 m alike. Three numbers are wrong. (a) '8 of 10 begin already carrying an inherited load (7.4 to 159.8)' mixes two definitions: inherited-only gives 6 of 10 at 7.35-156.91; total-accumulated gives 8 of 10 at 5.82-159.83. Neither gives the stated pair. (b) 'More than half of sub-main length fronts nothing' is 53.1 % only at the 60 m radius and falls to 48.4 % at 150 m - the headline flips sign inside the assumption's own plausible range, so it must be quoted as 'roughly half' with the radius stated. (c) The claim's NUMBERS say sub mains collect 2-15 lateral zones and its RULE says 3-15; the measurement is 2-15, and 5A-5|SM.4 takes exactly 2.

(a) 1,401 is not a measurement - it is an output of the 60 m allocation assumption, and the same pipe carries 1,209 / 1,399 / 1,570 / 1,704 properties at 30 / 60 / 100 / 150 m, with no radius matching more than 8.6 % of the plot layer. Pooled zone-length percentiles (m) 24.7 / 45.6 / 92.3 / 182.2 / 318.8 / 648.3, max 1,018.0 - exact. Chambers p50 4, p90 12, max 34 - exact. 131 single-pipe zones - exact. Zones per package 312/66/20/21/163 - exact. MISMATCHES: zero-plot zones **63**, not 59; properties p90 **27.9**, not 27.7. DISPERSION OUTSIDE 5A-1 (n=270), which the claim never reports: length p10 24.7 m, p25 49.5, median 132.1, p75 259.2, p90 402.3, max 916.4 - **p90/p10 = 16.3x**; chambers p10 2, median 6, p90 15, max 29 - 7.5x; properties fronted p10 1.5, median **9.8**, p90 33.1, max 105.7 - 22.8x; properties at outlet p10 2.0, median 11.6, p90 64.0, max 223.5 - 32.8x. 21 of 270 zones outside 5A-1 front zero plots.

DROP the sizing targets - do not size a zone at 130 m / 5-6 chambers / 10-15 properties. If a zone-size band is needed at all, quote the measured spread (25-400 m, 2-15 chambers, 2-33 properties at p10-p90) and label it a distribution, not a target.

correction: 'Small, repeatable unit' is refuted by the claim's own data once you look past the median. Outside 5A-1 the zone spans 16.3x in length from p10 to p90, 7.5x in chambers, 22.8x in properties fronted and 32.8x at the outlet. A quantity with that spread is not a repeatable unit and cannot be used as a sizing target - quoting only its median manufactures a regularity that is not in the data. Separately, 'roughly 10-15 properties' is not measured anywhere: properties fronted per zone are median 7.3 pooled and 9.8 outside 5A-1, while properties at the zone outlet outside 5A-1 are median 11.6. The 10-15 band splits the difference between two different statistics, and both move with the 60 m allocation radius. Two counts also differ: 63 zero-plot zones (not 59) and p90 27.9 properties (not 27.7).

claim: The built network is a tree except for exactly one loop - two laterals leave one chamber and rejoin six chambers later, 64 m of pipe involved. Everything else has out-degree 1.
numbers: TOPOLOGY REPRODUCED EXACTLY. 3,265 edges, 3,267 nodes, 3 components; a forest of three trees needs 3,264 edges, so surplus = **1**. Robust to the filter: on the full 3,267 Ex rows it is 3,267 edges / 3,268 nodes / 2 components, surplus still exactly 1. Exactly one chamber with out-degree 2 (5A-2-30-MH235); zero with out-degree >= 3; Kahn ordered all 3,265 pipes with 0 residue. LOOP TRACED PROPERLY: branch A = L011155 (36.5 m) via 5A-2-87-MH234 then zone 86, **8 pipes / 214.6 m / 7 intermediate chambers**; branch B = L011205 (27.4 m) via 5A-2-30-MH237 then zone 30, **7 pipes / 232.1 m / 6 intermediate chambers**; first common node 5A-2-SM.1-MH226. **Loop total 446.7 m of pipe and 13 intermediate chambers.** The claim's 64 m is 36.5 + 27.4, i.e. only the two pipes leaving the split.
design_rule: Publish edges, nodes and components every run and assert edges == nodes - components per subnetwork. Any surplus edge is a loop and must be named - and the report must give the LOOP LENGTH and the chamber count between split and rejoin, not the length of the two pipes leaving the split. A 447 m dual-feed with 13 chambers is a real thing to resolve on site; a 64 m one is a curiosity.
copy_or_not: COPY
correction: The topology counts, the single out-degree-2 chamber, the split and rejoin nodes and the branch identities are all exactly right, and the finding is robust to whether the two schematic rows are dropped. But '64 m of pipe involved' is wrong by a factor of seven: the branches rejoin after 8 pipes / 214.6 m and 7 pipes / 232.1 m, so 446.7 m of pipe and 13 intermediate chambers are inside the loop. The claim's own text - 'rejoin six chambers later' - contradicts its own 64 m figure, and nobody checked which of the two was right. If the reported figure is the one that reaches the design, a real 447 m dual-feed gets logged as a 64 m rounding note.

claim: There is a standard grade: 6.0 mm/m for laterals and 5.0 mm/m for the trunk; the 5.5-6.5 spike (31%) is a drawing-office habit, not a solver output.
numbers: Every quoted number reproduces to 2 dp: median 6.001, mean 8.889, p05 2.885, p10 3.646, p25 4.996, p75 8.555, p90 14.837, p95 25.406, max 160.946; length-wt 8.690; fall 549.26 m. Within 0.10 of 6.00 = 435 (20.31%), of 5.00 = 201 (9.38%), either 636 (29.69%). Bin 5.5-6.5 = 664 (31.0%). SLOPE_PCT cross-check max |diff| 3.6e-15. BUT trunk: 29 reaches within 0.10 of 6.00 vs only 21 within 0.10 of 5.00; trunk bin 5.5-6.5 (43 reaches, 27.5% of trunk len) ~ bin 4.5-5.5 (42, 29.5%); per-package trunk medians 5A-2 5.12, 5A-3 6.04, 5A-4 3.47, 5A-5 2.09. Above 6.5 mm/m (723 reaches, 33.0% of length) only 44.4% sit within 0.10 of a 0.5-rung against a 40% uniform expectation.
design_rule: Half-follows. The 6.0 rung for laterals is real (24.2% within 0.10, and the +/-0.10 window is TIGHTER than the 0.334 mm/m quantisation step at the 29.9 m median reach, so 20.3% is a floor not a ceiling). The rest does not: there is no 5.0 trunk rung, and there is no ladder above 6.5 mm/m across a third of the length. Snapping to '0.5 mm/m steps upward' is invented, not measured.
copy_or_not: COPY, narrowed: publish share of length on a 6.0 rung for laterals only. Do NOT declare a 5.0 trunk rung or a 0.5 ladder above 6.5 - name the upper third as continuously solved, which is what it is.
correction: One rung exists, at 6.0 mm/m, and it belongs to the laterals. The trunk has no standard grade: its modal bin is 6.0 (29 reaches) not 5.0 (21), and its four package medians span 2.09 to 6.04 mm/m. Above 6.5 mm/m - 33% of levelled length - the distribution is continuous, not laddered.

claim: The trunk is laid AT the Table 11 minimum (median 5.19 vs 5.00 mm/m required for DN200); 42 of 145 reaches, 31.1% of trunk length, are BELOW it. Pinning at the table minimum is right; being under it is not.
numbers: All reproduce exactly: trunk n=145, 4.53 km, all OD200, median 5.187, mean 5.594, p05 2.090, p10 2.457, p25 4.800, p75 6.051, p90 7.805, max 18.415. Below 5.00: 42 reaches = 31.1% of trunk length, 29.0% of count. OD160 below 5.00: 506 of 1,997 = 26.1% of OD160 length. Dead flat: exactly 5 reaches, 142.4 m, IDs L012129/L012721/L010893/L011085/L011149, all OD160 laterals. Adverse: 0. BUT the trunk IQR is 4.80-6.05 and per-package trunk medians are 5.12 / 6.04 / 3.47 / 2.09 - two of four packages sit MEDIAN-below the floor. And fitting Table 11's own power law (log-log slope -1.263 across 200-900 mm) extrapolates a 6.54 mm/m floor at 160 mm: 1,300 of 1,997 reaches = 65.8% of OD160 length is below that, not 26.1%.
design_rule: The gate follows; the premise does not. A hard gate of zero reaches below the tabulated minimum and zero dead-flat reaches is correct and cheap. But it must not be justified as 'copy their practice of pinning at the minimum' - there is no pinning to copy.
copy_or_not: DO_NOT_COPY confirmed, and extend it: the gate needs a defensible floor for OD160, which Table 11 does not supply. Adopt the extrapolated 6.54 mm/m as an explicitly tagged assumption per _BRAIN/05_GAPS.md, or refuse OD160 for anything but rider/property connections per G203-p22.
correction: The trunk is not laid at the Table 11 minimum - it is scattered around it (IQR 4.80-6.05, package medians 2.09 to 6.04, 29% of reaches below). The 26.1% OD160 figure is the wrong comparator and reads far too soft: against Table 11's own extrapolated 160 mm floor of 6.54 mm/m, 65.8% of OD160 length is under-graded.

claim: Sub-mains are laid FLATTER than the laterals they collect (median 4.04 vs 6.03 mm/m) in the same OD160 pipe; that decision is where the capacity failures live.
numbers: Tier medians reproduce exactly: trunk_main 145 / 4.53 km / 5.187; sub_main 322 / 9.92 km / 4.036 (p25 3.641, p10 2.885, mean 7.371, p95 26.577); lateral 1,675 / 48.75 km / 6.032. Diameter cross-tab exact: every sub_main OD160, every trunk OD200. STRENGTHENED at junction level (not a pooling artefact): 60 lateral->sub_main pairs, 71.7% laid flatter downstream, median 5.87 -> 4.07 mm/m; direction holds in all three packages with sub-mains (5A-2 6.67->5.30, 5A-4 6.98->4.06, 5A-5 6.00->3.65). Diameter steps up at only 20 of 2,139 pairs. BUT part-full Manning (D=0.150 m, n=0.011): tractive stress at the sub-main EXCEEDS the lateral's once it carries >~2.5x the flow - at 3x, 1.15 Pa vs 0.98 Pa; at 5x, 1.41 vs 0.98. Capacity is what actually falls: full-bore 14.0 -> 11.4 L/s, and at the G203-p27 d/D=0.65 cap 10.57 -> 8.65 L/s.
design_rule: Self-defeating as written. 'tau(downstream) >= tau(upstream) or diameter steps up' would PASS the exact reaches it was written to catch, because the flat sub-main has the HIGHER tractive stress. Table 11 itself encodes flatter minimums for larger pipes - a falling gradient down the hierarchy is normal practice, and is only a defect when the diameter fails to follow.
copy_or_not: DO_NOT_COPY confirmed, wrong reason. Replace the tau test with a capacity test: peak flow at d/D <= 0.65 (G203-p27 Tab 10), evaluated at every reach against its accumulated properties. Ban OD160 above the rider/property-connection role (G203-p22 sets OD200 minimum for lateral and main sewer) - the 686-property OD160 sub-main is a diameter fault, not a gradient fault.
correction: The measurement is right and robust; the mechanism and the rule are wrong. The flat sub-main is not a self-cleansing failure - its tractive stress is higher than the laterals' once it carries 3x their flow. The failure is pure capacity: 8.65 L/s at the depth-of-flow cap, in a pipe collecting hundreds of properties. The defect is that DIA_OUT never steps up (20 of 2,139 junctions), not that the grade steps down.

claim: Cover is a deliberate two-level design: laterals at minimum (median 1.40 m), mains deep (trunk 3.00 m, sub-main 4.01 m). Tiers are set at different depths on purpose so branches can drop into mains.
numbers: Every number reproduces exactly. ALL n=2,142: median 1.725, mean 2.177, p10 0.840, p25 1.050, p75 3.024, p90 4.383, p95 4.775, max 8.193 m. lateral median 1.395 (1,675 / 48.75 km); sub_main 4.010 (322 / 9.92 km); trunk_main 3.004 (145 / 4.53 km). Depth to invert median 1.885, p90 4.552, max 8.353 m. DEP_US/DEP_DS cross-check against US_GRD-US_INV: max |diff| exactly 0.000000 m. DIA_OUT present on all 2,142 (1,997 OD160 + 145 OD200), zero nulls. Independently corroborated by the drop data: at drop chambers the arriving pipe sits at 1.30 m cover and the leaving pipe at 3.15 m, against 1.88 m on both sides at flush chambers.
design_rule: Follows directly. A 2.6 m median spread between the lateral band and the sub-main band is exactly the depth budget a branch needs to be let into a main, and it is invisible in a single network-wide cover statistic. Publishing median cover per tier makes a flattened-tier design fail on sight.
copy_or_not: COPY confirmed. Note the one caveat: 5A-1 (32.25 km, 33.8% of built length) has no levels and no TM/SM tokens at all, so the two-level structure is measured on 5A-2/3/4/5 only and is unverified on a third of the network.

claim: 35.9% of levelled length is below the 1.30 m minimum cover, almost all of it laterals (44.9% vs 8.0% sub-main, 0.7% trunk) - a breach on 22.7 km, not a technique.
numbers: Every figure reproduces exactly on the claim's own reach-mean basis: <1.30 m = 790 reaches / 22.71 km / 35.9%; <1.00 = 477 / 13.57 / 21.5%; <0.60 = 21 / 0.59 / 0.9%; <0.50 = 10 / 0.28 / 0.4%. Excluding the 79 reaches (2.35 km) at exactly 1.000 m both ends: 711 / 20.36 km / 33.5% of the remaining 60.85 km. By tier 44.9 / 8.0 / 0.7%. By package 5A-2 47.8, 5A-4 47.0, 5A-3 32.3, 5A-5 27.9%. Shallowest L012630 at 0.3115 m. BUT the claim averages the two ends. On the SHALLOWEST end - the only basis on which a minimum-cover check means anything - it is 943 reaches / 27.17 km / 43.0% below 1.30 m; 702 / 20.28 km / 32.1% below 1.00 m; 60 / 1.74 km / 2.8% below 0.60 m; and 37 reaches / 1.13 km / 1.8% below the 0.50 m protected floor.
design_rule: Follows, and the rule itself exposes the error: 'no published reach below 1.30 m cover to crown' is a per-point test, so it must be measured at the shallow end. A stage that checks reach-mean cover will pass 153 reaches and 4.5 km that breach at one end.
copy_or_not: DO_NOT_COPY confirmed, and the case is stronger than stated. Specify the check at min(COVER_US, COVER_DS), publish per tier, and never cite the as-built as authority for a shallow pipe.
correction: The breach is worse than reported because reach-mean cover was used. Measured at the shallowest end: 43.0% of levelled length below 1.30 m (not 35.9%), 27.17 km (not 22.71), and 1.8% below the 0.50 m protected-pipe floor (not 0.4%) - a 4.5x understatement on the one threshold that has no engineering defence.

claim: They never dig deep: deepest cover 8.19 m in 63.2 km, nothing over 10 m, only 0.84 km over 6 m. The practical ceiling is ~8 m, so the real constraint is excavation cost, not the guideline.
numbers: Reproduces on the claim's reach-mean basis: max cover 8.193 m (L010919, 5A-2 sub_main, 30 m), max depth-to-invert 8.353 m, >6 m = 23 reaches / 0.839 km / 1.33%, >10 m = 0, >12 m = 0. Package p99 cover 4.89-6.60 m. BUT on END cover the maximum is 8.693 m, not 8.193, and only 2 reaches exceed 8 m at either end. The distribution says the ceiling is 6 m, not 8: 98.67% of length is under 6 m, p98 = 5.44, p99 = 6.02, p99.5 = 6.30, p99.9 = 6.98 m. The '8 m ceiling' rests on a single 30 m pipe - 0.05% of levelled length.
design_rule: The two-bar structure is right; the bar heights are wrong. Setting the layout-fault trigger at 8 m licenses a design to sit routinely in a band the built network touched once in 63.2 km. Set the trigger at 6 m, where the as-built p99 actually is, and keep 12 m as the absolute compliance bar (G203-p33 recommends approximately 10-12 m and cites excavation cost, so it is a recommendation, not a limit).
copy_or_not: COPY, with the trigger at 6 m not 8 m. Publish the count over 6 m as the layout-fault indicator, separately from the 12 m compliance check.
correction: The practical ceiling is ~6 m, not ~8 m: 98.7% of levelled length is under 6 m and p99 is 6.02 m, while over-8-m is one reach of 30 m. Max END cover is 8.69 m, not 8.19. And 'they never dig deep' is unverifiable on 33.8% of the built network - package 5A-1's 32.25 km carries no levels at all.

claim: The network is laid ~3.4 mm/m steeper than the ground in the median and genuinely follows the ground on only ~a tenth of its length: laid to a grade with the depth floating, the opposite of terrain-following.
numbers: Every headline number reproduces exactly. Laid median 6.001, surveyed ground 3.439, DEM ground 3.699; laid-minus-ground +3.394 (surveyed) / +3.553 (DEM). Surveyed at +/-1.0: FOLLOWS 227 = 10.7% of length, FLATTER 646 = 29.5%, STEEPER 1,269 = 59.8%. At +/-2.0: 17.9 / 26.4 / 55.7. At +/-5.0: 37.9 / 18.6 / 43.4. DEM at +/-1.0: 8.7 / 31.4 / 59.9. Depth change median +0.097 m per reach. The five sub-numbers (60.7% falling, 31.4% rising, 54.5% flatter-of-falling, ground median 8.62, laid median 6.03 and 5.96) do NOT reproduce on a plain sign split (I get 64.4 / 34.1 / 51.3 / 8.05) - they reproduce EXACTLY at an undisclosed +/-1.0 mm/m deadband on ground gradient, which the METHOD does not state. Only '61.5% of reaches get deeper' fails: I measure 62.56% (62.51% at a >1 mm threshold, 63.14% length-weighted).
design_rule: Follows. Three independent measurements agree - the tolerance sweep (10.7 -> 17.9 -> 37.9% following as the band widens from 1 to 5 mm/m), the DEM replication, and the fact that on uphill ground the pipe still holds a 5.96 mm/m median, which can only be bought with depth. Laying a standard grade per run and letting cover float between the minimum and the ceiling is what the data shows and is fewer decisions.
copy_or_not: COPY confirmed - but pair it with claim 5's floor. 'Let cover float' is only safe with a hard stop at 1.30 m, which the built network did not honour on 43% of its length.
correction: One method-disclosure gap and one small miss, neither touching the conclusion: the falling/rising sub-numbers require an unstated +/-1.0 mm/m deadband (on a plain sign split they are 64.4 / 34.1 / 51.3 / 8.05), and 'depth deeper on 61.5% of reaches' measures 62.6%.

claim: On steep ground they DO go steeper and shallower; W11b's 'REFUTED' verdict was wrong because it tested flood-hazard class (n=13) instead of ground steepness (n=293).
numbers: Every bin reproduces exactly on surveyed ground: >40 mm/m n=93 / 2.48 km / laid 11.05 / cover 1.54 / ddepth -0.96; 20-40 n=200 / 5.69 / 8.49 / 1.41 / -0.44; 5-20 n=613 / 18.23 / 6.06 / 1.56 / -0.07; -5..5 n=793 / 23.89 / 5.98 / 1.74 / +0.15; -20..-5 n=293 / 8.59 / 5.94 / 1.87 / +0.45; <-20 n=150 / 4.33 / 5.95 / 2.10 / +1.07. Steep-down (>20) vs level: 9.12 vs 5.98 mm/m laid, 1.42 vs 1.74 m cover, 44.6% vs 36.6% below 1.30 m. DEM >20: n=212 / 6.16 km / laid 10.06 / cover 1.25 / 50.3% below minimum. The AS_BUILT_TARGETS.md n=13 hazard-class basis is confirmed in the file (line 145, classes 4-6, 13 reaches). BUT: on 20-40 mm/m ground the pipe is laid at 8.49 mm/m - roughly a quarter of the ground slope, so 'steeper' is a mild trend, not terrain-following; and this is the same slice where 44.6-50.3% of length already breaches minimum cover.
design_rule: Half follows. Raising the laid gradient toward 9-11 mm/m on steep ground is measured and safe. 'Accept that cover will trend down to the minimum by the bottom of the slope' is not: in the built network that same behaviour put 44.6% of steep-down length (50.3% on DEM-steep ground) BELOW the 1.30 m minimum, which is exactly what claim 5 tags DO_NOT_COPY. The two rules as written contradict each other. And 'take the surplus fall at a chamber' is NOT what they did - claim 9's own data puts drop chambers on the FLATTER ground (arriving ground gradient 1.62 vs 3.81 mm/m signed).
copy_or_not: COPY the gradient half only. Reject 'accept cover trending to the minimum' - it is the mechanism that produced the claim-5 breach. Re-word: raise the gradient toward 9-11 mm/m AND trigger a drop structure before cover reaches 1.30 m, which is a departure from the as-built, not a copy of it.
correction: Measurement fully confirmed on all six bins and both binnings; the AS_BUILT_TARGETS.md retraction is justified (n=13 hazard classes vs n=293 ground-steepness reaches). The proposed rule is not: its second half licenses the 1.30 m cover breach that claim 5 calls a guideline violation on 44.6% of that same steep length.

claim: A drop structure here is a TIER MISMATCH device, not a hillside device: 120 of 121 drops >0.60 m at junctions, arriving pipe at minimum cover into a 3.15 m main, on ground FLATTER than average.
numbers: Every number reproduces exactly: 2,139 pairs / 1,877 chambers; negative 6 (0.28%), flush 1,874 (87.61%), 0.005-0.10 45 (2.10%), 0.10-0.60 93 (4.35%), BACKDROP 84 pairs / 81 chambers (3.93%), VORTEX 37 / 37 (1.73%). Rates 1.329 backdrop/km, 0.585 vortex/km, 44.8 and 19.7 per 1,000 chambers. Drops >0.60: p25 0.93, median 1.45, p75 2.11, p90 2.76, max 4.19; 27 at 2-3 m, 8 at 3-4 m, 2 over 4 m. Junction: 120/121 and 37/37 against a 24.0% base rate. Arriving cover 1.304 vs leaving 3.146 m; flush 1.884 both sides; 49.6% vs 32.4% at or below 1.30 m. Zero trunk mains as arriving pipe. BUT the tier flow refutes the headline: 19 of 37 vortex drops are SAME-TIER (18 lateral->lateral + 1 sub_main->sub_main), and 82 of 121 drops >0.60 m are same-tier. And the 'flatter ground' evidence is an artefact of using SIGNED gradient: on ABSOLUTE ground gradient drops sit at 6.40 mm/m against 7.52 at flush chambers - a 15% difference, not the 2.35x the signed figures imply.
design_rule: The operational rule survives; the label does not. Allowing drops only at junctions and publishing non-junction drops as a hard failure is well supported (4x enrichment over a 24.0% base rate, and the enrichment is not circular - a pass-through chamber has no reason to step). But the offset must be sized on DEPTH, not tier: same-tier drops run 1.01 m arriving into 2.47 m leaving, cross-tier 2.17 into 4.19 m, so a single '1.5 m tier offset' number does not describe either population.
copy_or_not: COPY the junction rule. Drop the tier-mismatch framing and the single 1.5 m offset - size the drop from the receiving pipe's actual invert, and publish the same-tier/cross-tier split so a lateral-into-lateral drop is not mistaken for a hierarchy feature.
correction: It is a DEPTH mismatch device, not a tier mismatch device - the claim's own tier table refutes its headline: 19 of 37 vortex drops and 82 of 121 drops over 0.60 m join pipes of the SAME tier, most of them lateral into lateral. And drops are not on notably flatter ground: 6.40 vs 7.52 mm/m absolute ground gradient. The signed comparison (1.62 vs 3.81) measures direction mix, not steepness.

claim: 28% of the system's descent is taken at chambers, not pipes - 215 m of invert step against 549 m of pipe fall. Drop structures are a first-order part of how this network gets downhill. NAMA's 28% is the calibration point.
numbers: Reproduces exactly: pipe fall 549.26 m over 63.20 km (8.69 mm/m length-weighted); chamber fall counting max(drop) once per chamber 214.96 m across 245 chambers; share 214.96/(549.26+214.96) = 28.13%. Sensitivity: summing all positive pairs gives 221.52 m -> 28.74%; counting only drops >0.60 m gives 193.47 m -> 26.05%, i.e. 90% of the chamber fall comes from ~120 chambers out of 1,877. BUT the basis is the levelled 63.20 km only, which claim 12 (same author) establishes is the worse two-thirds; package 5A-1 (32.25 km, 33.8% of built length, best-behaved on both uphill measures at 20.3% and ratio 0.110) has no levels and contributes nothing.
design_rule: The metric is worth publishing; the calibration value is not safe as stated. 'Near zero means it dug for its fall, far above ~30% means it dropped out of a bad layout' is a reasonable two-sided reading, but 28.1% is an upper-biased anchor - it is measured entirely on the four packages with the worst uphill behaviour, and it is dominated by 120 chambers.
copy_or_not: INFORM_ONLY confirmed. Publish the share, but quote it as '28.1% on the levelled 63.2 km of packages 5A-2/3/4/5' and never as a network-wide figure. The comparable number for 5A-1 is unmeasurable, and that is a gap, not a zero.
correction: The 28.13% is arithmetically exact but its basis is not the system. It covers 66% of the built network by length, excludes the one package whose terrain and uphill statistics predict it needed the fewest drops, and 90% of it comes from ~120 chambers. As a calibration point it is biased high by an unknown amount.

claim: Gradient changes at only about a third of plain chambers - one grade is carried through roughly two chambers on average - and 99.3% of pass-through chambers are laid flush.
numbers: Every quoted number reproduces exactly: 1,623 pass-through chambers; grade held within 0.05 = 1,041 (64.1%), 0.10 = 1,128 (69.5%), 0.25 = 77.3%, 0.50 = 83.3%, 1.00 = 85.8%. |dGRAD| median 0.029, p75 0.200, p90 3.401. Flush 99.26%, median step 0.0000 m. Chains at 0.10 tolerance: 1,014 covering all 2,142 reaches, median 1 reach, mean 2.112, max 27; length median 34.8 m, mean 62.3, p90 142.1, max 852.9; 63.6% single-reach. Reaches with >2 vertices 38 (1.77%). BUT the headline arithmetic is wrong: mean 2.112 REACHES per chain is 1.112 CHAMBERS, and the median chain of 1 reach passes through ZERO chambers. And the topological ceiling - chaining through every pass-through link regardless of grade - is 519 runs, median 3 reaches, mean 4.13 reaches (3.13 chambers), median 85.8 m.
design_rule: Good advice, mis-tagged. Because 69.5% survival is per-chamber, it compounds: over the 3.13-chamber run the topology actually offers, a grade survives only 0.695^3 = 34% of the time, which is why the mean chain is 2.11 reaches against a ceiling of 4.13. The built network therefore holds a grade through about half the run available to it. 'Lay every pass-through chamber flush' is a genuine copy (99.26%); 'set the grade per run' is an improvement on the as-built.
copy_or_not: Split the tag. COPY the flush rule (99.26% measured, and the 0.7% that step are the defect). Keep 'grade per run' as a design decision, labelled as an improvement - publishing it as [COPY] misrepresents what NAMA did.
correction: One grade is carried through 1.112 chambers on average, median ZERO - not 'roughly two chambers'. The claim converted reaches to chambers without subtracting one. Against a topological ceiling of 3.13 chambers per run, the built network re-grades at roughly two-thirds of its opportunities, so 'set the grade per run' is a departure from the as-built, not a copy of it.

claim: The 34.1% / 0.483 target is measured on the levelled two-thirds, which is the WORSE two-thirds; over all 3,265 built pipes on the DEM it is 29.88% uphill with ratio 0.265, so the as-built bar is HARDER than the published target.
numbers: Every number reproduces exactly. Levelled/surveyed: 34.10% uphill, climb 256.6 m (4.06 m/km), descent 531.0 m (8.40 m/km), ratio 0.483 - matches the published target in AS_BUILT_TARGETS.md line 20/22 exactly. Levelled/DEM: 34.77%, ratio 0.422. All 3,265 built on DEM: 29.88%, climb 252.7 m (2.65 m/km), descent 952.7 m (9.98 m/km), ratio 0.265. 5A-1: 1,123 pipes, 32.25 km, 20.30% uphill, ratio 0.110. DECOMPOSITION the claim did not do: the same reaches on the DEM give 34.77% - statistically identical to the surveyed 34.10%. So changing the ground source moves nothing; the entire drop from 34.1% to 29.9% comes from ADDING package 5A-1.
design_rule: Follows in outcome, wrong in diagnosis. Comparing like with like is right, but the confound is not the measurement basis - the decomposition proves the DEM and the survey agree on the same pipes to within 0.7 pp. The variable is package composition: 5A-1 alone drags the whole-network figure down, and it is a structurally different package (no levels, no TM/SM tokens, entirely typed 'lateral').
copy_or_not: INFORM_ONLY confirmed. Score a W12 against 29.88% / 0.265 over 95.45 km on the DEM - but say the reason is that the bar now includes 5A-1, not that the ground source changed.
correction: Numbers exact and the conclusion holds, but the stated cause is wrong. The claim's own figures decompose it: surveyed 34.10% vs DEM 34.77% on identical reaches means the measurement basis contributes ~0.7 pp of the 4.2 pp gap. All of the rest is package 5A-1, which is not a measurement question but a composition one.

claim: The uphill fraction is set by terrain, not design skill: across five packages the uphill share moves 20% to 39% in EXACT inverse order of ground steepness, so a single uphill target for a whole town is meaningless.
numbers: The per-package numbers reproduce exactly (5A-1 11.16 mm/m -> 20.30% / 0.110 / 32.25 km; 5A-3 10.41 -> 38.37 / 0.408 / 3.45; 5A-2 10.07 -> 27.83 / 0.303 / 20.01; 5A-4 10.05 -> 28.10 / 0.243 / 5.04; 5A-5 5.92 -> 39.39 / 0.587 / 34.70; surveyed 27.97 / 32.22 / 31.69 / 38.15). But 'exact inverse order' is false on the claim's own table: 5A-3 is the SECOND steepest and has the SECOND HIGHEST uphill share. Spearman rho = -0.70, p = 0.188 on n=5 - not significant. Drop 5A-1 (which the brief warns must be stated separately) and rho falls to -0.40. At a finer grain - 6 ZONEs of >=1 km on the same DEM - rho = -0.20, p = 0.704: the relationship vanishes. Three of the five packages separating 5A-1 from 5A-5 differ by 0.02-1.11 mm/m in median ground gradient, inside the 16.9 mm/m DEM-vs-survey noise the same author measures in claim 14. And the tier line pools 5A-1: 'lateral 30.59% / 0.264' becomes 37.40% / 0.463 with 5A-1 stated separately, which REVERSES the ordering - laterals then run uphill MORE than the trunk (34.18%), not less.
design_rule: Does not follow. Fitting an acceptable-uphill target as a function of median |ground gradient| calibrated on five points with rho = -0.70 at p = 0.19, which collapses to -0.20 at zone grain, is a one-parameter model on noise. Shipping it would set per-subnetwork targets that are effectively arbitrary - and a target set too loose on flat ground buys exactly the pumping stations the rule claims to prevent.
copy_or_not: Reject the calibration. The weaker conclusion is safe and worth keeping: a single town-wide uphill target is not defensible, so report uphill share per subnetwork as an observation and let the engineer judge it. Do not derive a threshold from these five points.
correction: The ordering is not exact and the correlation is not significant: Spearman -0.70 at p = 0.188 on n=5, -0.40 without 5A-1, and -0.20 (p = 0.70) across 6 zones of >=1 km. Two packages (5A-1 steep/low, 5A-5 flat/high) drive the whole appearance and 5A-1 is the package the data brief says must never be pooled. The claim's own tier line does pool it: laterals are 37.4% uphill with ratio 0.463 once 5A-1 is separated, not 30.6% / 0.264, which flips them from better than the trunk to worse.

claim: The 0.5 m DEM cannot grade an individual reach - sampled at two end nodes of a 30 m reach its disagreement with surveyed ground has sd ~18 mm/m against a 6 mm/m design gradient, and our pipeline grades against exactly this surface at exactly this spacing.
numbers: Every number reproduces exactly. Residual DEM minus recorded ground, n=4,284: median +0.247, mean +0.297, p05 -0.478, p95 +1.115 m. Gradient disagreement n=2,142: median -0.070 (unbiased), mean -0.205, sd 16.896, |diff| median 6.546, p10 -15.423, p90 +14.964; correlation 0.5788. By length: <20 m (n=168) sd 25.75; 20-30 (n=958) 17.95; 30-50 (n=1,001) 13.71. Median reach 29.9 m. Orientation independently verified: MAE 0.941 m under the assumed US->DS vs 1.136 m flipped. NEW: the three length bins fit an independent point-noise model with sigma_z = 0.27 / 0.32 / 0.39 m, consistent across a 2.7x span in baseline - strong evidence the disagreement really is per-point vertical error. AND the signal is smaller than the noise: median |surveyed ground gradient| is 7.49 mm/m against a 16.90 mm/m disagreement.
design_rule: Follows, and the consistent sigma_z across three length bins strengthens it - the error scales as 1/L, which is exactly why two-point sampling fails and along-reach regression fixes it. Flagging outfalls, station thresholds and wadi crossings for survey rather than trusting the raster follows independently, from the +0.25 m median bias alone.
copy_or_not: COPY confirmed. This is the most directly actionable finding in the set: the pipeline currently grades against a surface whose per-reach gradient signal-to-noise is below 0.5.
correction: Numbers exact and the rule follows, but the blame is misattributed. If this were added DEM noise, DEM gradient variance would exceed surveyed. It does not: var(surveyed) = 406.2 vs var(DEM) = 242.8, sd 20.15 vs 15.58. So a substantial part of the 16.9 mm/m is the 2006 survey being wrong or the ground having changed in twenty years, not the raster. (2) The gate as written would also FAIL a correctly sized design in which flow bands happen to coincide with tiers. (3) Scope overstated in one direction and understated in another: the 1,675 'recorded laterals' are only 60% of the 2,798 laterals (the rest are unsized 5A-1); and NAMA's own unbuilt SUREKHA Design rows in the same shapefile use TWELVE diameters (200 x66, 315 x16, 250 x13, 500 x7, 700 x6, 600 x5, 1000 x4, 1400 x4, 900 x3, 800 x2, 1200 x2, 400 x1). So 'diameter is a tier label' characterises the 2006 BUILT scheme, not the client's design practice - do not present it to NWS as the latter.

claim: A flow path from head to outfall changes size at most once, ever: 173 of 264 measurable paths step exactly once, 91 never step, none steps twice; median path 69 reaches, median 23 sized reaches per path.
numbers: STEP COUNTS REPRODUCED EXACTLY: 486 heads (in-degree 0), 486 paths walked head to outfall, 264 with >=2 sized reaches, steps 0 -> 91 paths, 1 -> 173, 2+ -> 0. correction: Three corrections. (1) '23 sized reaches per path' is a denominator switch: the step statistics use the 264 measurable paths, the 23.5 uses all 486. On the 264 it is 61, and the median run at one bore before the step is 32 reaches. The finding is STRONGER than claimed, not weaker - one bore for 32 consecutive reaches, not 23. (2) 'Not one path steps twice' is arithmetically FORCED, not discovered: with exactly two diameters in the entire network (claim 1) and zero decreases anywhere (claim 2), at most one step per path is a theorem. Presenting it as an independent finding triple-counts one fact. (3) The rule collides head-on with claim 12's. I tested it: computing the required diameter at each reach's own laid gradient and comparing consecutive reaches, the built network's own geometry would demand 87 size changes, of which 15 are MID-RUN at a plain pass-through chamber. claim: The sizing is INVERTED in places: OD200 trunk reaches carry as little as 27 properties while OD160 sub-mains carry up to 1,401. 17% of trunk is oversized, 11% of sub-mains undersized against the other class's median.
numbers: REPRODUCED EXACTLY (single-successor accumulation): 25 of 145 OD200 trunk reaches = 17.2% carry less than the median OD160 sub-main (181.8 properties). 36 of 322 OD160 sub-mains = 11.2% carry more than the median OD200 trunk reach (698.2). Smallest-loaded OD200 = L011321, zone 5A-3-TM, 26.7 properties. Largest-loaded OD160 = L012069, 5A-5-SM.2, 1,400.9 - a 52.4x load difference in favour of the SMALLER pipe. Mann-Whitney AUC of OD200 over OD160 by load = 0.9467 (claim 0.947).
design_rule: Hard schedule check: no reach may be larger than a reach downstream of it, and NO REACH MAY CARRY MORE FLOW THAN ANY LARGER-DIAMETER REACH ANYWHERE IN ITS OWN PACKAGE. A single inverted pair should fail the export.
copy_or_not: DO_NOT_COPY - upheld.
correction: The measurements stand; the second half of the rule is hydraulically wrong and must not be made an export gate. Capacity goes as D^2.67 * S^0.5, so a steeper small pipe can legitimately carry more than a flatter large one - flow-versus-diameter ordering is not an invariant of a correct design. I tested the rule on the built network itself: in package 5A-3 it flags 16 OD160 reaches that carry more than the least-loaded OD200 reach and that PASS their own Colebrook capacity check - 16 of the 38 reaches it flags network-wide, 42%, are false positives. Blocking an export on those would stop a sound design. Keep the FIRST half (DIA(reach) <= DIA(successor)) as the hard gate - that is claim 12's monotonicity check - and make the second half an audit on UTILISATION (q/Qcap <= 1 everywhere), which is the quantity that actually has to hold.

copy_or_not: DO_NOT_COPY the built sizing - upheld. But the RULE needs one correction before it is adopted.
correction: Three corrections, one of them material to our own design. (1) MATERIAL: the rule imports the WRONG infiltration allowance. G201-p72 gives 10% of WW flow for an EXISTING inland network and 720 L/d per KM OF SEWER for a NEW one - the two constants are side by side in W11b/py/w11b/asbuilt.py with those exact comments. The screen is right to use 10% on NAMA's 2006 pipes; carrying it onto W11b applies the existing-network allowance to a new network. On the same 2,137 reaches the swap moves the fail count from 238 to 213 (median peak-flow ratio 0.911) - an 11.7% swing in the gate's own output. Use 720 L/d/km on our design. (2) The required-diameter tail is understated: the 9 reaches / 0.311 km labelled OD400 need OD500. I verified it - they fit at OD400 only if you keep d/D at 0.65 there, and G203-p27 Table 10 drops the cap to 0.50 above 350 mm. At 0.50, all 9 fail OD400. (3) Today's loaded count is 1,817 not 1,815 (laterals 1,371 not 1,369); 5.1% is unaffected. Also worth stating with the gate: AS_BUILT_TARGETS.md calls this a screen that 'ranks pipes, it does not model them' with SewerGEMS as the referee - promoting it to a blocking export gate goes beyond what its own authors said it can carry.

copy_or_not: DO_NOT_COPY - upheld.
correction: Nothing to correct, and it survives the obvious rebuttal I tried against it. I expected the -0.334 to be an artefact of tier composition (sub-mains are both heavier and flatter, so pooling two tiers manufactures the correlation). claim: OD160 sub-mains cannot reach self-cleansing velocity even running completely full: median full-bore velocity 0.555 m/s, best case 1.14x = 0.63 m/s, below the 0.75 m/s G203-p26 requires at peak.
numbers: REPRODUCED, including the two figures I first could not match. Full-bore Colebrook velocity at the laid gradient, median: lateral OD160 0.6802 m/s, sub_main OD160 0.5555, trunk_main OD200 0.7322 - exact. Maximum v/V for a circular pipe = 1.1400 at d/D 0.813 (I computed the curve, not quoted it), so 0.5555 x 1.14 = 0.633 m/s - exact. Velocity at the saturated peak by bisection on the proportional-discharge curve: sub_main median 0.5616 m/s, 51.6% of 318 below 0.75, 127 surcharged; trunk median 0.7639, 26.2% of 145 below 0.75, 66 surcharged - all exact ONCE their surcharge convention is used, which is q > FULL-BORE Q, not q > the 1.0757 maximum of q/Q at d/D 0.938. On the stricter (more correct) convention: sub_main 109 surcharged, median 0.5773; trunk unchanged at 66.

copy_or_not: DO_NOT_COPY - upheld.
correction: Numbers stand; two corrections. (1) The '% below 0.75 m/s' UNDERSTATES the problem, because a surcharged reach is counted as not-below when it has no free-surface velocity at all. On the reaches that do have a solution, 164 of 191 sub-mains - 85.9% - are below 0.75 m/s. Report it as 'below 0.75 or surcharged', which is 291 of 318 sub-mains (91.5%). (2) The RULE'S REASONING IS FALSE AS WRITTEN and would be quoted back at us. 'A smaller bore does not buy velocity - at a fixed gradient it loses it' is true only at FULL BORE. At a fixed FLOW - which is the case the 'go smaller to scour' argument is actually about - the smaller bore is FASTER: I measured it at S = 6 mm/m, q = 3 L/s, ID 150 gives 0.563 m/s against ID 188's 0.552; at q = 1 L/s, 0.411 against 0.400. The genuine argument against going small is CAPACITY, not velocity: at 20 L/s the 150 bore surcharges while the 188 runs at 0.893 m/s. Rewrite the rule to say that, or it is wrong on the physics.

claim: The trunk-main verdict survives its one assumption, but only at saturation: across the plausible 176-192 mm internal bore the saturated failure rate stays 54-67% while today's swings 20-39%.

But add the thing the sensitivity table conceals: at ID 188 mm, 28 of the 145 trunk reaches sit between 0.9 and 1.1 utilisation, and at 192 mm it is 28 again - the failure COUNT is knife-edge on an unrecorded number. The defensible statement is 'most of the trunk is at or past capacity at saturation on any plausible bore', not a count. The rule to publish ID and pipe class is right and I would strengthen it: publish the utilisation too, so the next reader can see how many reaches sit on the knife edge.

numbers: THE NON-REPRODUCTION IS CONFIRMED: I measure 93 over capacity today and 1,400.9 / 538.5 on L012069. But the claim's premise - that nobody can name the filter - is wrong, and I found it. W10/docs/research/HIERARCHY_RULES.md section 10 carries both: line 437 gives the 686, and line 447 gives '110 pipes cannot pass peak flow at all. 57 sub-main and 53 trunk pipes SURCHARGE.' The 110 is a SURCHARGE count (q > full-bore Q), not an over-capacity count against the Table 10 d/D cap - a different metric. On the current basis I measure 28 surcharged today (26 with 720 L/d/km infiltration), by tier 0 lateral / 28 sub-main / 0 trunk - against their 57 sub-main and 53 trunk. And no accumulation variant I tried yields 686: 1,400.9 saturated, 538.5 at electricity-account occupancy, 962.2 as a raw plot count.

copy_or_not: INFORM_ONLY - upheld, but the action is wrong.
correction: The right action is not 'drop them' but 'mark them superseded and name the basis'. Both numbers come from HIERARCHY_RULES.md section 10, computed with the W10-era model (hydra.pipe_state, PLOT_QADF_M3D, 720 L/d/km infiltration) built on ONE PROPERTY PER PLOT at OR 6.0 - the load basis the project's own CLAUDE.md records as RETIRED at W10 Phase 1.3, when the saturated Qadf moved from 49,700 to 74,700 m3/d (1.291 x 1.207 = 1.558). That is why they do not reproduce, and it is also why the 110 cannot simply be relabelled: it is a different METRIC on a retired BASIS, two changes at once. Project rule 12 keeps a superseded number as the record of what was done, so the fix is a correction note against README.md line 88, W11a_BUILD_BRIEF.md lines 154-156 and HIERARCHY_RULES.md section 10 saying which basis produced them and what replaces them (93 over capacity / 28 surcharged today; 1,401 saturated / 538 today). Deleting them would destroy the audit trail that let me find this in twenty minutes.

claim: Two sizing habits are worth copying and only two: the network never narrows in the direction of flow, and every size change sits at a chamber that is already a junction.
numbers: REPRODUCED EXACTLY: 20 diameter changes, 20 increases, 0 decreases; 20 of 20 at a node with in-degree >= 2; 0 mid-run; 17 distinct manholes, every one a trunk-main chamber (5A-2 x7, 5A-3 x6, 5A-5 x4).
design_rule: Enforce BOTH as export gates: DIA(reach) <= DIA(successor) everywhere, and every diameter change must coincide with a junction chamber.
copy_or_not: COPY - but only the first gate is safe to make blocking. Downgrade the second to a reporting check.
correction: The measurements stand; the pair of gates does not, for three reasons I tested. (1) The second gate COLLIDES with claim 3's proposed gate. Computing the required diameter at each reach's own laid gradient, the built network's own geometry would need 87 size changes, 15 of them MID-RUN at a plain pass-through chamber. A design that sizes honestly to accumulated flow WILL cross a capacity band between junctions on a long run; a hard 'changes only at junctions' gate would force it to oversize the whole run or to plant a fictitious junction. Monotonicity is the hard gate; junction-placement is a reporting check with a stated allowance. (2) The second habit carries almost no independent information here - all 20 changes are the SAME event, a lateral or sub-main meeting the trunk, and a tier boundary into a trunk is a junction by construction. It is claim 1 restated, not a second finding. (3) 'Never narrows' is measured on 2,139 of 3,261 pairs (65.6%); the other 1,122 are wholly inside unsized 5A-1. And with exactly two diameters in the network, 'zero decreases' is close to vacuous - there is one narrowing that could physically have occurred and it did not. Copy the monotonicity gate on its own merits (it is what a contractor expects and it costs nothing), not on the strength of this evidence.

claim: No subnetwork crosses the trunk; zero pipe-pair intersections without a shared manhole; all 24 catchments discharging into a trunk do so at their own nearest chamber; every non-trunk join lands at chainage offset 0.0 m.
numbers: MY FUNNEL (reproduces theirs exactly): SEWERLINE_IBRI.shp 3,396 rows -> STATUS='Ex' 3,267 (111.567 km) -> drop 2 schematic by measured m-per-vertex >100 (L012750, L012751, 16.117 km) -> 3,265 pipes, 95.450 km. Note W10_existing_built.shp IS the STATUS='Ex' subset (I verified FEATUREID overlap 3,267/3,267), so 'no STATUS column' is correct. CROSSINGS: STRtree over 3,265 pipes gives 3,769 intersecting pairs, 0 without a shared US/DS_MHID; separately the 'crosses' predicate returns 0 X-shaped pairs of any kind. TRUNK JOINS: 23, not 24 — lateral->trunk 13, sub_main->trunk 8, trunk->trunk 2. NEAREST-CHAMBER: 23/23 outlet chambers are their zone's minimum-distance chamber to the receiving package's trunk. ELSEWHERE-APPROACH: of the 21 non-trunk zones, 0 have any other chamber within 25 m of the trunk (min d_min_others = 28.2 m). CHAINAGE: 8 of 21 at exactly 0.0 m, 19 of 21 within 5 m, max offset 20.4 m (zone 5A-3|10, receiving 5A-3-TM-MH5035 while the nearest point is 20.4 m upstream). Trunk chainages: 5A-2 2.264 km/72, 5A-3 1.075/38, 5A-4 0.678/20, 5A-5 0.512/15.
design_rule: KEEP the planarity check: no two reaches may cross without a shared chamber — 0 in 95.45 km, so any crossing W12 publishes is a defect. DOWNGRADE the nearest-chamber check: keep it, but as a cheap sanity test only, and set the real test on CHAINAGE (join chainage vs the chainage of the zone's nearest point on the trunk) at <=5 m, which the built network passes 19/21 and fails twice. Do not use 'exactly 0.0 m'.
copy_or_not: COPY (planarity), COPY-WITH-WEAKER-TOLERANCE (join position)
correction: Three errors. (1) There are 23 direct trunk joins, not 24: trunk-zone-into-trunk-zone happens twice (5A-2|TM->5A-4-TM-MH6033, 5A-3|TM->5A-2-TM-MH79), not three times; the fourth trunk zone 5A-5|TM is a terminal and 5A-4|TM discharges into a sub main. (2) 'Every non-trunk join landed at chainage offset 0.0 m' is false: only 8 of 21 are exactly 0.0 m, 19 of 21 are within 5 m, and one is 20.4 m off. Their chainage test also silently omitted the 5A-4 trunk (20 pipes, 0.678 km) — they listed only 125 of the 145 trunk pipes. (3) '1 of 24 within 5 m / 10 m, 11 of 24 within 25 m' does not reproduce. Against the receiving package's own trunk, 0 of 21 non-trunk zones has another chamber within 25 m. Their two sub-5 m hits are the two TRUNK zones measured against a union that contains their own geometry — a self-distance artefact, distance 0.0 by construction; the '11 of 24 within 25 m' comes from measuring zone PIPES rather than chambers, a different quantity from the one the claim states. FINALLY, the surviving nearest-chamber result is near-tautological: the ratio of second-nearest to nearest chamber distance has median exactly 2.00 (range 1.48-2.86), i.e. the runner-up is one manhole spacing further back. The test confirms that zones are linear chains ending perpendicular at the trunk — which the topology already tells you — not that a routing choice was made. No join chamber sits ON the trunk: separation is 11.8-42.8 m, median 25.5 m.

claim: The corridor is the plot-boundary street reservation, not the mapped road centreline. 90 % of built length is within 8 m of a road centreline OR a plot boundary; only 7.4 % runs inside a plot; the apparent off-corridor problem is an incomplete road layer, chiefly in 5A-5.
numbers: 49,351 samples at 2 m, weights summing to 95.4498 km. Within 8 m: census 44.83 %, rc2 46.56 %, W11b DXF 47.73 %, union of three 57.16 % (all four EXACT matches). Union at 15/25/50 m: 71.13 / 79.19 / 94.82 %. Plot boundary alone (16,002 MoH plots in extent) 76.85 %. Road-OR-plot-boundary: 8 m 90.51 %, 15 m 95.31 %, 25 m 97.32 %. Inside a plot polygon 7.52 % = 7.180 km (lateral 8.60, trunk 1.83, sub-main 1.32). Off-road >25 m: 19.866 km = 20.81 %, of which 80.5 % within 8 m of a plot boundary. 5A-5 off-road >25 m: 14.011 km, 80.8 % within 8 m of a boundary, median 2.01 m — all three EXACT. Length-weighted p90 distance to the road union 43.0 m. CONTROLS I RAN AND THEY DID NOT: 40,000 random points within 100 m of the network are 55.81 % within 8 m of a plot boundary and 48.63 % inside a plot; the 183.33 km road choice set is 53.87 % within 8 m of a boundary and only 3.04 % inside a plot. In 5A-5 specifically, 25,000 random points near the network give 57.7 % within 8 m of a boundary at median 6.48 m, against the pipe's 80.8 % at median 2.01 m.
design_rule: KEEP: route on the public reservation between plots and use the plot-boundary graph as the corridor where the road layer is silent. claim: 9. The rising main is 1.48x its straight-line distance - 3.24 km bought to follow roads and stay off the wadis - and 7.1 % of its route crosses class 4-6 flood ground.
